div.head: Cn 1027 2
div.ab: Hanc quidem profectionem Deo iam olim deuoueram, sed pro negotiis regni et causis impedientibus huc usque perficere non poteram.
Hanc quidem profectionem Deo iam olim devoveram, sed pro negotiis regni et causis impedientibus huc usque perficere non poteram.
Long ago I had vowed this journey to God, but, on account of affairs of State and other delays, I had not been able to perform it until now.
I had long ago vowed this journey to God, but I was not able to perform it until now because of the affairs of the kingdom and other causes of hindrance.
div.note: Latin only (Cnut's letter of 1027, c. May; Latin translation c. 1070–1100, the Old English original is lost). Liebermann's text is from Florence of Worcester (ed. MGH SS XIII 126), compared with Ox (Oxford, Corpus 157 p. 329) and William of Malmesbury II 183; text in column T. Liebermann gives no German translation.
Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 276 (November 2026; read twice from the page images and against the text layer). His superscript letters, which refer to his Erklärungen, are left out.

note.seg: Auch viele andere Fürsten aus Europas Norden und Nordwesten pilgerten damals nach Rom. Bei Cnut verband sich dem unbezweifelbaren religiösen Beweggrunde Politik (vgl. u. 10); Steenstrup Normannerne III 351

Many other princes from the north and north-west of Europe also went on pilgrimage to Rome at that time. In Cnut's case policy was combined with the undoubtable religious motive (cf. below 10); Steenstrup Normannerne III 351

Vorher ging ein Kampf gegen Norwegen und Schweden im Herbst 1026 (s. u. 13b); ebd. 347 ff.; Larson Canute 213 ff. Cnut reiste aus Dänemark über Flandern. Das weiss auch das Encom. Emmae 520, dessen Verfasser ihn zu St. Omer auf der Hinreise sah, und Heimskringla; Mon. Germ. 275. 262 f. 362. Schiffbruchsgefahr berichtet Gocelin Vita s. August. Cant.

This was preceded by a war against Norway and Sweden in the autumn of 1026 (see below 13b); ibid. 347 ff.; Larson Canute 213 ff. Cnut travelled from Denmark via Flanders. This is known also to the Encom. Emmae 520, whose author saw him at St Omer on the outward journey, and to Heimskringla; Mon. Germ. 275. 262 f. 362. Danger of shipwreck is reported by Gocelin Vita s. August. Cant.
